title: The Tea of 1926
synopsis: In Chinatown, a tea house has kept Eleanor's red tin for a hundred years.
Mrs. Lee will give it only to a careful reader.
And a TV crew wants to film everything.
goal: Find Eleanor's tin, earn it, and open it.

options.label: The tin with a rabbit and a sun
options.feedback: A rabbit, yes. But the card says under a full moon, not a sun.

options.label: The tin with a fish and a moon
options.feedback: A full moon, yes. But what animal sits under it?

options.label: The tin with a rabbit and a moon

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene) in the tea room: the framed card on the wall describes the tin's lid; the tin shelf opens once it is read. The three tins are the same red tin; only the lid picture changes (a rabbit or a fish, a full moon or a sun).
The right tin is also the case's evidence picture (ev_red_tin, 1024x1024); the two wrong tins are drawn from it.

Coordinates measured on the made tea_room.png (1536x1024, sha256 1b2ee811…) with a 50px grid sheet (season_factory). The framed card hangs left of centre; the shelf's area starts right of the lantern (the tins under the lantern belong to no spot), and the counter's starts above the teapots, below the shelf; the lantern is its body and its tassel.

learning.objective: 액자 카드의 'a white rabbit under a full moon'을 읽고 세 깡통 중 뚜껑 그림이 맞는 것을 고른다.
expressions: a white rabbit under a full moon
Not a sun. Not a fish.

play.title: The Red Tin
story: The tea house smells of jasmine and old wood.
Mrs. Lee, the owner, bows. "My grandmother knew Eleanor."
Outside, a TV van parks. Dexter Vance waves at the window.
play.letterIntro: A framed card on the wall says:
play.letter:
Eleanor's tea is kept in a red tin.
On its lid: a white rabbit under a full moon.
Not a sun. Not a fish.
— Mei Lee, 1926
play.question: Which tin is Eleanor's?
hints: Find the framed card on the wall and read it first.
Look at each lid. You need a rabbit AND a full moon.
transition: Mrs. Lee takes down the tin with the moon and the rabbit.
"Not so fast," she smiles. "First, my grandmother's question."
Dexter and his camera operator, Nora, come inside.

lines.text: Hello again! Mind if we film? It's for the children!
How did you know we were here?
A good treasure hunter always knows! Go on, look around.

discovery.title: THE MOON AND THE RABBIT
discovery.detail: Eleanor's tin has waited here for a hundred years. Three dials keep it shut.

notes: Letter: Mei Lee's 1926 recipe, written out of order with first, after, once and last. 'Add milk' is a decoy: the recipe says never.

clueInputs.note: Each friend asks one question: this is Mrs. Lee's.
The tin is found; now it must be earned.

learning.objective: first of all, after, once, last를 읽고 1926년 방식의 차 만드는 순서를 맞춘다.
expressions: But first of all, warm the pot.

play.title: Eleanor's Tea
story: Mrs. Lee puts a teapot in front of you.
"My grandmother's question: make Eleanor's tea the 1926 way."
Nora films your hands. Dexter watches the tin.
play.letter:
Never add milk to Eleanor's tea!
Pour the tea into cups last, after three minutes.
Hot water goes in only after the leaves.
But first of all, warm the pot.
The leaves go into the pot once it is warm.
play.question: Make Eleanor's tea. Put the steps in order.
hints: One line says what you do first of all.
Read 'after' and 'last'. Do you need every card?
transition: The tea is perfect. Mrs. Lee gives you the red tin.
Then she opens a small drawer.
"My grandmother wrote about Eleanor's secret, too."
play.orderFeedback: Find what you do first of all. Then read 'once' and 'after'.

evidence.inscription: Never add milk to Eleanor's tea!

notes: Letter: a page of Mei Lee's 1926 diary. The six-note song (first half on the brass bird, last half in Eleanor's family) is the key of Act 3: Otto remembers the first half (Case 06), Rosa keeps the last (Case 08).

learning.objective: 일기의 'the first three notes'와 'the last three notes'를 구별해 읽고, 노래의 뒤쪽 세 음이 어디 있는지 찾는다.
expressions: She put the first three notes on a brass bird.
The last three notes stay with her own family.

play.title: Mei Lee's Diary
story: The diary page is thin and brown.
Mrs. Lee reads it out in a soft voice.
play.letter:
Today my friend Eleanor left her red tin with me.
She told me a secret about her Lark.
It sings a song of six notes.
She put the first three notes on a brass bird.
The last three notes stay with her own family.
"Only my whole song wakes my Lark," she said.
play.question: Where are the last three notes of the Lark's song?
hints: Find the line about the first three notes. The next line is the answer.
Who keeps the last three notes?
transition: The Lark needs its whole song: six notes.
Three are on a brass bird. Three are with Eleanor's family.
"Does Eleanor still have a family?" Maya wonders.

clue.title: The Six-Note Song
clue.value: 3 NOTES ON THE BIRD · 3 WITH THE FAMILY
clue.note: The Lark wakes only to its whole song. Half is on a brass bird; half is with Eleanor's family.

evidence.name: Mei Lee's Diary
evidence.description: A page from Mei Lee's diary of 1926.
evidence.inscription: Only my whole song wakes my Lark.

discovery.title: A SONG IN TWO HALVES
discovery.detail: To wake the Lark, you need both halves of its song.

notes: Eleanor's lid card asks for three numbers from the trail so far: the clock's four faces (Case 02 M2), the two red lanterns (Case 02's egg note), the four letters of EAST (Case 02 M3).

clueInputs.note: First number: the clock has four faces.
Second number: two red lanterns over the door.
Third number: EAST has four letters.

learning.objective: 지난 단서(시계의 얼굴, 등불, 달걀의 단어)를 다시 읽고 how many 질문에 답해 숫자 4·2·4를 맞춘다.
expressions: How many faces has the clock in the great hall?
How many letters open my egg?

play.title: The Three Dials
story: You sit on the step under the red lanterns.
The tin has three small dials.
A card is tied to the lid.
play.letter:
My tin opens with three numbers.
First: How many faces has the clock in the great hall?
Second: How many red lanterns hang over my friend's door?
Third: How many letters open my egg?
— E. H.
play.question: Turn the dials to Eleanor's three numbers. Then open the tin.
hints: Your Notebook has Eleanor's question about the clock, and her egg note.
Count the letters of the word that opened the brass egg.
transition: Inside the tin is Eleanor's next note.
Nora films it very close. Dexter reads it over your shoulder.
The next stop is the Brooklyn Bridge.

feedback.324: Count the clock's faces again. Read Eleanor's question in your Notebook.
feedback.414: Look over the door again. How many lanterns does the egg note say?
feedback.434: How many red lanterns? Read the egg note again.
feedback.423: Count the letters of the egg's word again.

play.orderFeedback: These numbers fit, but not in this order. Clock, lanterns, then the egg.

evidence.name: The Tin Note
evidence.description: Eleanor's note from inside the red tin.
evidence.inscription: Stop under the first stone tower. My brass bird sits on the bench there.

ending.text: The note says: walk the great bridge to Brooklyn.
Under the first stone tower, a brass bird sits on a bench.
The bird holds the song's first three notes.
Sorry... I have to go now.
ending.speaker: nora_bell

ending.text: Why does Nora look so worried?

hook: Everyone in the tea house heard the tin note. Who will reach the brass bird first?

learningGoal.title: Reading a description and steps in order
learningGoal.titleKo: 묘사 읽기와 순서: first of all, after, last

intro: Chinatown. Narrow streets, red lanterns and the smell of dumplings.
Doyers Street bends like an elbow.
There stands the Golden Lantern Tea House.
play.caseSummary: Mrs. Lee's tea house kept Eleanor's red tin, with a rabbit under a full moon. You made Eleanor's tea the 1926 way and earned it. Mei Lee's diary told the Lark's secret: its six-note song is in two halves. The tin opened with 4, 2, 4 and sent you to a brass bird on the Brooklyn Bridge. Dexter and Nora heard it all.

notes: Dexter and Nora film the tin note: that is how the thief knows the bench (Case 04), the question the detective asks in Case 06's final.
The six-note song (s4_ep03_c3) is paid off in Case 06 (the first half, remembered by Otto), Case 08 (the last half, Rosa's family) and Case 12.
